wintercity_e09_entry.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_entry.text: The works' written offer arrived on Day 871 in an ordinary envelope, carried by a messenger paid to obtain a receipt. Yue signed for delivery, not acceptance. Inside were the proposed duties, hours, pay, source rules, and a note inviting her to inspect the workplace before deciding. Gao Shen's seal stood at the bottom. It could establish who had made the offer. It did not establish that the terms suited her, or transform the messenger's arrival into the first day of a job.

wintercity_e09_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_002.text: The full offer covered fourteen four-hour mornings from Day 874 through Day 887, at two copper per hour. Weekly payment after completed hours would total fifty-six copper each week. The work concerned stock comparisons and source-labelled internal notes, with no heavy lifting. Six named afternoon bench observations were included for the work's own comparisons; they were not private personal-practice sessions. Yue could not take the works' instruments, cylinder residuals, or client papers home merely because the appointment had an attractive total.

wintercity_e09_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_003.text: A confidentiality clause protected private methods and client identities. A separate paragraph preserved the right to report a specific safety concern through the authorized public process without releasing unrelated private detail. Another clause restricted public teaching from the works' methods. The exit procedure allowed departure with notice and payment for completed hours, while requiring actual return of loaned sources. Yue read the paragraphs together. A worker should not have to choose between a vague oath of silence and an equally vague promise that any disclosure would be forgiven.

wintercity_e09_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_004.text: The offer included a narrower alternative if she wanted only a short trial. It covered six mornings from Day 874 through Day 879, four hours each at the same rate, for forty-eight copper after completion. The tasks used public-stock comparisons and excluded private method bench access. The appointment would end without an implied renewal. Its smaller income bought less time under the employer's conditions. Yue could compare that actual option with the full one instead of negotiating against an imaginary freedom the factory had never offered.

wintercity_e09_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_005.text: Ning had separately posted six mornings of public-map and service-reference copying for the same dates, three hours each at two copper per hour. That finite office job would pay thirty-six copper and had its own source custody, with no factory bench access. The public fund had been approved before Yue received the works' offer. Another qualified applicant could take it if she chose the factory. A meaningful alternative needed an actual budget and vacancy, rather than appear costlessly when a protagonist disliked a powerful person's terms.

wintercity_e09_006.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_006.text: She placed all three scopes on the inn table. Wen read the practical exit line; Jia counted the completed hours. Neither told her which one defined a courageous cultivator. The full offer provided substantially more paid work and a private comparison setting. The trial kept the commitment shorter without granting the private bench. The public job provided less money and more ordinary afternoon freedom. Yue would have to decide which obligations she could carry, including the unchosen work and access that would remain unavailable.

wintercity_e09_007.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_007.text: Before the works' visit on Day 871, Yue sat beside the public basin with the letter's last page folded beneath her notes. The source rules were clear enough to read, but she wanted a moment before another person's proposed future filled her morning. A boy sailed a bark boat through a shallow puddle near the lip. It turned in circles because one edge was thicker. He kept trying different pushes instead of demanding that the water recognise his intention. Yue watched until he found a straighter path.

wintercity_e09_008.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_008.text: She remembered the lower recruitment terrace, where her own root had once seemed too faint for anyone to bother measuring carefully. Those years had not become meaningless because a Foundation owner could now offer her ordinary clerical work. They had also not placed her beyond ordinary needs. Her paid room, meals, and friendships were part of the life she had wanted to reach. She could accept useful work without pretending every shift was a disguised spiritual test or proof that her ambition had failed.

wintercity_e09_009.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_009.text: The pendant lay under her robe, the cord familiar against her collar. She checked its knot because a loose knot could lose a possession. It gave her no opinion about the offer. Yue almost laughed at how readily a tired mind wanted an object to decide a difficult question. The envelope contained actual hours and conditions; her body carried a measured small circuit; her purse held finite earned money. Those were enough to begin a decision without making a silent stone its authority.

wintercity_e09_010.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_010.text: When she rose, the bark boat had lodged beneath a twig. The boy asked the basin keeper before reaching across the service opening. The keeper used an ordinary hook, then gave him the boat on the clear side. Yue walked away before seeing whether the next attempt went straight. She had no claim to turn the whole afternoon into a parable that ended exactly where she needed it. Her own appointment waited with its own actual question, which a child's boat could not answer.

wintercity_e09_011.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_011.text: Before deciding, she went to the works' visitor office. Its stone floor was warm near the return pipe and cold beside the outer door. The receptionist gave her a visitor token whose end time was printed plainly. She could inspect the offered workplace under escort, not roam the factory. Yue asked to see the desk used for the comparison work and the source cupboard. Those places mattered more to a clerk's actual day than the impressive public tower pictured in the advertisement.

wintercity_e09_012.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_012.text: The comparison room had a low table, two scales, and a locked cupboard for client sources. The supervisor showed Yue where the ordinary chair could be adjusted and where workers could leave the desk for a break. No lifting duty was hidden behind the phrase help as needed. She asked who moved containers. The assigned store workers did. If a later task changed that division, it required a new agreed scope; a busy morning would not amend it by convenience.

wintercity_e09_013.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_013.text: At a bench beyond the table, a technician was checking an uncharged control housing. Yue remained behind the visitor mark. The full appointment's included bench observations would let her compare specified records with the technician's permitted demonstration. They would not make her the operator or owner. Her own recent public application result, whatever its exact scope, remained separate. The ordinary stock job did not require her to claim a useful signal or interruption qualification she had not completed. The supervisor read that point from the actual duty sheet.

wintercity_e09_014.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_014.text: Gao Shen joined the visitor inspection midway through it. He asked what she had thought of the room. Yue said the explicit lifting division and source boundaries were useful, and asked why the public teaching restriction extended beyond the term. He replied that private methods remained private after wages ended. She agreed about ownership and asked whether the restriction also covered her independent nonconfidential observations. He called for the precise paragraph rather than answer from a flattering general assurance.

wintercity_e09_015.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_015.text: The paragraph protected the works' identified method sources and client particulars, while reserving her own independently acquired observations. Yue asked that the offer's source inventory make the identification practical. Gao Shen agreed to attach the inventory before acceptance. He did not offer her ownership of the private method. She did not ask him to bless every future account she might write. A concrete boundary could be negotiated without requiring either person to concede that all the other's interests were unreasonable.

wintercity_e09_016.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_016.text: He told her careful clerks were harder to retain than strong hands. The works could purchase another cylinder; it could not purchase a worker's judgement as a finished object on a shelf. Yue liked the recognition and distrusted how quickly liking it could change her reading of the contract. Gao Shen was speaking as an employer who wanted a reliable worker. The compliment could be sincere and serve his interests at the same time. She thanked him and returned to the source-return clause.

wintercity_e09_017.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_017.text: The owner described a further permanent position that might follow satisfactory work. Its pay and conditions were not on today's page. Yue said she would treat it as a possible future offer, not part of the present fourteen mornings. He smiled and accepted that answer. She would not borrow for a season on the basis of a possible position, or claim he had promised one if it never arrived. The proposed temporary work had enough real value and enough real limits to be judged on its own.

wintercity_e09_018.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_018.text: When she asked about the public comparative event, Gao Shen's expression changed from recruitment to mild curiosity. He thought the city overvalued fine procedural words when a service ultimately needed power. Yue said a room also needed permission, staff, fuel, and a route people could use. He did not dispute those necessities. He said none would compensate if the operator lacked capacity for the load. She had no truthful answer that made her small circuit equal his joined Foundation, and did not invent one.

wintercity_e09_019.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_019.text: He invited her to inspect the event's final public conditions once they were posted. He did not enrol her as a contestant through employment. A clerk could accept or decline the job while remaining an ordinary visitor to the demonstration. Yue wanted that distinction on the contract, and the supervisor confirmed it in writing. It would be easy for an audience to confuse an employee's presence with a duty to perform. She left with that particular confusion removed before it could become a convenient command.

wintercity_e09_020.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_020.text: At the gate, Yue returned the visitor token and kept only her own permitted notes. Later on Day 871, Ren offered a two-morning grain reconciliation, five hours each on Days 872 and 873, from the early bell until before noon. Its deadline rate was three copper per hour, fifteen after each completed shift. The fixed thirty came from Ren's business account. Yue accepted after checking that local contract reading could occur afterward and no factory job began before Day 874.

wintercity_e09_021.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_021.text: On Day 872, Yue asked Chen Rui for an independent contract reading by correspondence through the public desk. He was not physically in the city, and Ning did not promise an immediate answer. The ordinary route could deliver a limited written question and receive a reply after its real travel time. Yue instead paid the local reading clerk two copper for the immediate bounded reading available today. A familiar advocate could help later, but distance prevented him becoming a conveniently instant voice at the table.

wintercity_e09_022.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_022.text: The local reader, Qin Lu, checked the proposed hours, pay, confidentiality boundary, and source inventory. She was an ordinary registered contract reader, not a spiritual examiner. She pointed to a line requiring a worker to report a custody discrepancy promptly and asked whether Yue understood the practical burden. Yue did. The reader also asked whether a late payment had a written complaint route. The works' draft supplied one, but the first response period extended beyond an ordinary weekly meal budget.

wintercity_e09_023.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_023.text: After Qin Lu's reading on Day 872, Yue remained at the public table while the clerk packed her tools. Qin Lu said she disliked being asked whether a contract was good in one word. A clause could be clear and onerous, unclear and intended kindly, or useful for one person and wrong for another. Yue asked whether that made every answer too complicated to act on. The clerk said no; it made the reader ask which obligation the person could actually carry. She kept the local reader's questions beside her own practical calendar.

wintercity_e09_024.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_024.text: Before that contract reading on Day 872, Yue had completed Ren's first five-hour reconciliation and received fifteen copper. She checked physical delivery tallies against the receipts, returning the business sheets. The following morning had to be worked for its separate fifteen. Qin Lu offered an account of leaving a copying post when its hours no longer suited her care duties. Yue listened without requesting private history. Both women's finite work had calendars rather than a promise to be endlessly available.

wintercity_e09_025.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_025.text: A man waiting nearby wanted the clerk to promise he would win a fee dispute. Qin Lu offered to identify the clause and the actual evidence he held. The promise was unavailable. He hesitated, then paid for the limited reading. Yue left before his private papers opened. The public room's shared tables required attention to who could see what. She carried the clerk's practical question about obligations, leaving his hoped-for victory and actual source file with their proper reader.

wintercity_e09_026.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_026.text: Outside, she bought a small bowl of roasted chestnuts. A seller warned that one batch had cooled and offered it at a lower price. Yue chose the cooler batch because she would eat it soon. The first nut was firm, the second sweet, and the third difficult to peel. The purchase had an ordinary uneven pleasure that did not need a moral conclusion. She kept the shells in the waste paper until she reached the basket, then went back to the contract office.

wintercity_e09_027.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_027.text: Yue took that question back to the visitor office. The supervisor agreed to provide a wage receipt on the actual payment day and a written reason for any disputed hours, with an ordinary expedited review route. He did not agree to pay unworked time or waive every possible custody claim. Yue could value the amendment without calling it a full victory over the works. It improved the review of actual hours and preserved the need to show those hours and any disputed source return.

wintercity_e09_028.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_028.text: At the public desk, Ning confirmed that the separate six-morning copying vacancy remained open until the posted deadline. Yue asked what happened if she chose another job. Ning would appoint the next qualified applicant. The public work and its funding would continue without waiting for Yue to become available. Yue was relieved by that answer and a little saddened by how replaceable it made her. An institution that depended on one traveller for every useful task would have been a weaker alternative, not a greater tribute.

wintercity_e09_029.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_029.text: She checked the next week's lodging before accepting any employment. Mrs. Fen offered the current weekly room through Day 877 at twelve copper. Afterward, a longer quiet shared-room interval would cost eight copper a week, because Yue now knew the other occupants and could take the less flexible notice period. The rate change came with actual terms, not a reward for cultivation. Yue paid the current week and copied the later offer for review. Food remained a separate ordinary expense.

wintercity_e09_030.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_030.text: Wen asked if the full factory pay tempted her. Yue said it did. She wanted money enough that declining an attractive offer would be a real choice with a cost, rather than a performance staged by someone already secure. Wen wanted customers enough to consider a difficult repair, then decide its actual price. They understood each other without arriving at the same answer. Jia pointed out that fourteen mornings were also fourteen mornings unavailable for another job. Yue wrote the overlap into her calendar.

wintercity_e09_031.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_031.text: On Day 873, Yue completed Ren's second five-hour morning and received fifteen copper. Thirty was now paid for ten hours at three each, with all business papers returned and that term closed. Later, the revised factory inventory and wage-review clause arrived. Its private identifiers and return procedure were clear, with her own independent notes retained. The apparatus visits remained observations, not personal powered trials. A better contract and real wages had changed her choices while her physical capacity remained at its tested stage.

wintercity_employment_choice.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_choice.text: She considered between the full factory appointment, the shorter factory trial, and the separately funded public copying work. Each would change paid hours, source access, afternoon time, and who could ask her for a report. She would not accept all three overlapping mornings or collect wages from the unchosen jobs. Her completed earlier work and travel reserve remained hers whichever offer she selected. A new commitment would need its own actual labour rather than receive legitimacy merely because she had read it carefully.

choices.text: Accept fourteen factory mornings and work-only private comparison access.
Take the six-morning factory trial without private bench access.
Decline both factory posts and take the separately funded public copying job.

wintercity_e09_033.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_033.text: The accepted job entered her calendar under its proper source and end date. The unchosen vacancies stayed with their actual employers, who could offer them to other qualified people. Yue informed the relevant desk promptly, sparing it the expense of waiting for an answer it would not receive. She kept copies of the accepted terms and any refusal receipt. Reading alternatives had been useful; only the selected appointment could authorize her later working space, pay, and source custody.

wintercity_e09_034.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_034.text: At supper, she told Wen and Jia what she had chosen without turning the explanation into a judgement of their livelihoods. Jia still wanted to know whether the pay covered the longer room. Wen wanted to know when they could walk to the festival. Yue answered those practical questions from the actual calendar. The job did not own every evening, but ordinary tiredness might still change how many plans she could keep. She would tell them early if she needed to rest.

wintercity_e09_035.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_035.text: On Day 874, she arrived at the selected workplace before its posted start. Her current job identity determined the door she could use and the sources she could touch. The public street remained available to everyone. A factory employee's pass did not authorize an unrelated public delegate role; a public copying worker could not borrow the private comparison cupboard. Yue carried the relevant paper and left the unused offer copies in the trunk, where they could remain comparisons without masquerading as passes.

wintercity_e09_036.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_036.text: The first morning's tasks were deliberately ordinary. She checked a current source label against a copied entry, identified an unresolved addition, and asked the supervisor before altering the total. The accepted appointment defined which particular sources those tasks used. She would not copy private methods into a public service form or treat a public notice as proof of a confidential client's full arrangement. The day's reviewed page established four or three actually worked hours under the applicable job, not the maximum she might someday earn.

wintercity_e09_037.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_037.text: At lunch, she met Rao Jun outside the station. The glazier had received a partial credit for the chipped replacement pane, with the remainder still disputed under the delivery terms. He was satisfied that the shop window had opened and annoyed about the unfinished claim. Yue asked whether he wanted her to copy the public procedure reference. He said he already had it. She accepted the answer. Competent workers could use help selectively without requiring a traveller to become their advocate through every difficulty.

wintercity_e09_038.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_038.text: Jun asked if she worked for the factory now. Yue gave the actual selected answer, distinguishing the full appointment, short trial, or separate public job. He wished her well and said his own window term would end after the festival. A job's employer could shape who a person knew and which sources she saw. It need not convert every friendly conversation into alliance or hostility. They parted when his customer arrived, leaving the claim where it belonged with its actual parties.

wintercity_e09_039.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_039.text: In the afternoon, Yue read the final public contest conditions. The comparative event would include a direct bounded counter-movement station, separately inspected for its declared participants and input ranges. Its independent supervision, ordinary mechanical limit, padded side runout, and paid first-aid interval had been arranged before any application from her. A participant could release or withdraw under the posted rule. The strongest completed result would win. No clause promised the smaller circuit a compensating triumph for being sincere or procedurally careful.

wintercity_e09_040.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_040.text: The station's public note described Gao Shen's qualified larger range and the lower range available to a Qi Gathering small-circuit participant. Equal notice did not mean equal physical ability. The owner would measurably have more usable capacity for the counterforce than Yue. She could compete within her own permitted limit and lose. She could also decline an application, leaving no contested result. Today she only read the conditions. The next week would bring the actual public challenge and a decision made with more than a recruiter’s compliment in her ears.

wintercity_e09_041.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_041.text: On Day 875, her selected morning work continued. She felt the ordinary fatigue of careful copying and stood during the permitted break. Her circuit remained unused in the clerical task. The supervisor did not ask her to demonstrate a larger personal output to earn the agreed hourly pay. The record's correction needed sources and arithmetic, not spiritual pressure. Yue was glad the job's value came from what she could actually do, though she knew she still wanted the dignity of being seen as more than a clerk.

wintercity_e09_042.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_042.text: That wish unsettled her more than Gao Shen's confidence. She had spent years trying to cultivate, then earned each step through recovered work. Yet a larger capacity did not necessarily make every other skill feel larger in an audience's eyes. She caught herself imagining a brilliant moment at the public station that would silence every condescending remark she had heard. The image was satisfying and unsupported. Her small circuit's ceiling had not changed because she wanted a room full of people to recognise the years behind it.

wintercity_e09_043.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_043.text: She walked to Min Tuan's yard after lunch and paid two copper for another ordinary lesson. Tuan asked her to rehearse the step-back under a gentle permitted push from a padded board, with no qi and no heavy load. She managed one step and tangled the next with her own heel. He stopped the exercise before increasing pressure. Yue admitted she had been thinking about spectators. Tuan said the floor would not become wider because spectators wanted her to hold her place.

wintercity_e09_044.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_044.text: He showed her the actual open space and asked where she would put a foot if she chose to release early. Yue identified it. The next slow attempt worked better. The lesson could prepare a retreat path; it could not make her equal a Foundation practitioner. Tuan had no authority to judge her spiritual technique. He could still tell her that an ordinary body needed somewhere to go when a contest ended, and that pride was a poor substitute for knowing the space.

wintercity_e09_045.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_045.text: That evening, the inn's long shared-room offer remained on the table. Yue asked the other occupants whether their sleeping schedules would work with her accepted job. One guest rose before dawn; another wanted quiet after the late room closed. They agreed a practical light arrangement and a place for trunks. Yue accepted the eight-copper weekly rate beginning Day 878 under its longer notice. The cheaper bed would help the actual budget while reducing her freedom to depart without paying the stated notice interval.

wintercity_e09_046.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_046.text: On Day 876, Ning delivered Chen Rui's later reply to the bounded correspondence question. It came after Yue had already made her employment decision, and did not rewrite that decision's date. He confirmed the source boundary question was sensible and suggested preserving the inventory for any later dispute. He could not advise on private clauses he had not been sent. Yue read the answer as useful limited advice from a distant advocate, whose timing and incomplete sources remained part of its value.

wintercity_e09_047.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_047.text: She sent a brief acknowledgement through the ordinary route, paying one copper. Chen Rui was not compelled to keep working because she had once asked a question. If a later hearing required his services, it would need its own scope and consent. Yue retained the local reader's two-copper receipt and the distant reply separately. A familiar name could offer continuity without becoming a permanent unpaid authority at every turning point of her city life.

wintercity_e09_048.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_048.text: At the square, the festival troupe had completed its papered lantern row. The dancer with the damaged strap now used a repaired boot and still kept one turn slower until her ankle felt fully reliable. The director accepted the revised movement for the first performance. Yue liked its unevenness. Wen wanted to see the whole dance before deciding. They could enjoy a repaired performance without declaring that the original discomfort had been a useful gift arranged for the audience's aesthetic education.

wintercity_e09_049.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_049.text: After the troupe rehearsal on Day 876, Wen asked Yue to walk along the lower market. A fish seller had fewer fresh trays because the upstream road had delayed his morning delivery. He labelled the older accepted stock by its real receipt date. Customers could choose it within its actual safe interval or leave. He did not let the city heat his stall beyond the inspected setting to make the fish look livelier. Warmth that suited a person could harm the food somebody sold.

wintercity_e09_050.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_050.text: Wen wanted a small fish for supper and chose one from the dated tray after checking its condition. Yue bought only vegetables. Their shared walk did not require identical purchases. At the inn, they would cook during the paid preparation interval with enough room for another guest's task. Wen said she hoped the public contest would not consume every conversation until festival day. Yue admitted she had been thinking about it too often. She wanted her friend's company to remain worth more than an audience for that ambition.

wintercity_e09_051.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_051.text: They stopped where the lantern light would eventually reach the wall. Wen described the repair she most wanted to finish before the festival, a child's umbrella with a handle painted like a fox. Yue told her about the ordinary step-back that still felt awkward under a gentle push. Neither story was impressive to a stranger. Between them, both were useful. Wen said a fox handle deserved a careful eye too. Yue promised to look at it when the actual client permitted the display.

wintercity_e09_052.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_052.text: Returning to the inn, Yue felt the difference between being understood and being admired. Wen did not know every measure of her circuit, and had no need to. She knew that a public challenge could make Yue forget an ordinary supper. Yue would have to keep choosing the smaller evening promises as well as the larger ambition. That did not guarantee she would always choose wisely when the crowd came. It gave her a person to answer honestly afterward, whatever the physical result might be.

wintercity_e09_053.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_053.text: On Day 877, Yue finished the selected week's last morning before the next different phase of the accepted job. The actual completed hours went to the relevant wage record. A full factory appointment would continue, a short trial would still have two mornings left, and the public job would follow its own end date. She kept those clocks distinct. Tomorrow's paid work could not be assumed from today's satisfaction, and a trial would not renew because its room felt familiar.

wintercity_e09_054.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e09_054.text: She put the job pass or public source receipt beside the next day's map. The city's private works and public desks had both offered useful ordinary tasks, with unequal pay and access. Her choice had selected one real position among them. Ahead lay a public challenge whose physical result would not be determined by this employment paper. Yue closed the source inventory, checked her repaired robe, and left the lamp low. She wanted to read the next offer of admiration as carefully as she had read this one.

wintercity_employment_factory.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_factory.text: Yue accepted the full fourteen-morning factory appointment. The two weekly payments would total one hundred twelve copper only after the fifty-six actual hours were completed. Her shift began on Day 874 and the term ended after Day 887, with the attached exit and source-return procedures. She signed the revised inventory rather than an undefined claim over every note she might ever write. The six work-only bench observations were dated 874, 876, 878, 880, 882, and 884. None authorized private personal practice.

wintercity_employment_factory_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_factory_002.text: She declined the separate public copying vacancy and informed Ning before its deadline. The office would appoint another qualified person. Yue gained actual internal source access under the works' confidentiality boundaries, and lost the public job's free afternoons on the six observation dates. Her full factory pass did not provide a citywide delegate mandate or a general apparatus licence. The private teaching restriction would continue for the identified method sources after wages ended, while her own independent observations remained hers.

wintercity_employment_factory_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_factory_003.text: The visitor office issued the time-limited employee pass and a cupboard custody sheet. Yue took neither an instrument nor a fuel cylinder. More income and a private work setting made the appointment attractive; they also gave the employer a practical right to ask for particular reports within the accepted duties. Her consent now had consequences that a pleasant inspection alone had not created.

wintercity_employment_probation.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_probation.text: Yue chose the six-morning factory trial, Days 874 through 879, four hours per morning at two copper per hour. Its forty-eight copper would be paid for completed work at the term's end. The trial used public-stock comparison sources and granted no private method bench observation. Yue signed the limited inventory and exit terms. No permanent post or extra morning was implied. She would have to make a new decision if the employer later offered another scope.

wintercity_employment_probation_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_probation_002.text: She told Ning she had accepted the trial, so the separate public job could go to another qualified applicant. The factory issued a pass limited to the ordinary comparison desk. It would not open the private source cupboard or laboratory door. Her afternoons remained outside the works' observation schedule, with no apparatus role supplied by that freedom. Choosing less commitment preserved time and avoided particular private-source duties, while leaving the full appointment's additional pay and access unavailable.

wintercity_employment_probation_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_probation_003.text: Yue kept the trial's end date visible on her own calendar. If the work went well, satisfaction would not automatically renew it. She owed accurate public-stock pages and actual return of the few loaned comparison sheets. The limited job was real employment with a finite payment, rather than an observation dressed up as wages or a quiet claim to every benefit of the full offer.

wintercity_employment_public.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_public.text: Yue declined both new factory appointments and accepted the independently funded public copying job. It covered six three-hour mornings from Day 874 through Day 879, at two copper per hour, for thirty-six after completed work. Ning issued the public source-custody sheet and the finite office appointment. Yue would copy service maps and reference summaries available under their public rules. She had no factory pass, private method access, or included bench observation. The lower income was an actual cost of this choice.

wintercity_employment_public_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_public_002.text: The works' visitor office acknowledged her refusal without altering wages from any earlier completed receiving job. Those payments were already hers. Yue retained her own notes from the permitted workplace inspection but returned the unaccepted full inventory copy under the offer's instructions. She would not use a rejected offer's seal as an access token. If a later city task needed private works material, the actual owner and audience would have to authorize it separately.

wintercity_employment_public_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_employment_public_003.text: Her afternoons remained available for ordinary errands, rest, or another properly scoped task. wintercity_employment_first_factory_001.speaker: narrator
